newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Feb capacity utilisation falls to 81 pct.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Feb capacity utilisation falls to 81 pct.

text.p: Production capacity utilisation in South Africa's manufacturing sector was 81 percent in February from November's 82.8 percent, figures from the Central Statistical Service (CSS) showed on Tuesday.
Year-on-year the figure showed a small increase of 0.2 percent with the largest contributors the beverage, footwear, basic non-ferrous metal and machinery and equipment industries.
Insufficient demand was blamed by manufacturers as the main reason for the 19 percent under utilisation rate in February.
Raw materials also were a factor in the utilisation gap.
At 94.1 percent, the non-ferrous metals industry showed the highest utilisation rate in February, followed by petroleum products at 90.1 percent.

The pottery and porcelain ware sector fared worst at 71.3 percent utilisation. Motor vehicle manufacturers also were near the back of the pack at 71.7 percent and was the beverage industry at 72.2 percent.
The CSS samples capacity utilisation rates four times a year for the months of February, May, August and November.
